bio: A meal at Cuines, 33 is an experience in its own right. As you first relax in the lounge, you are immersed in the soothing colour scheme, a genuine ode to Japanese minimalism. Right from the first bite, Edwin Menue’s cosmopolitan creativity can be tasted in creations like pani puri with razor clams and a dashi, illustrating just how his delicate touch underscores the entire establishment. The chef and the lady of the house, Fleur, then invite you to make your way into the dining area, whose counter seats sixteen. There you have a bird’s eye view of the chefs’ painstaking handiwork as they curate crisp veal sweetbread lacquered in sesame seeds and served on velvety mashed potato with a drizzling of vanilla and coffee oil and shavings of marinated egg yolk.
